title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person without her knowledge or consent. The person who deployed the system obtained photographs from the victim's private social media account, used AI to generate explicit deepfake images, and then distributed them across multiple social platforms using fake accounts to conceal his identity. The victim only learned of this when third parties informed her the images were circulating.

This is a case of a tool deployed for harm outside any legitimate use case. It would have been caught by platform moderation if the distribution channels had been monitored for this type of abuse, or if the AI system itself had included safeguards against creating non-consensual intimate imagery. It was not caught until the victim herself reported it to law enforcement.

It is not established whether the AI system used had any built-in protections against this type of misuse, or whether any platform had notice of the abuse before the victim reported it.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create explicit morphed images. He then circulated this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail IDs to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her manipulated photographs and videos were being shared through Discord servers. She reported the case to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During investigation, police analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake accounts to Bansal. He admitted to knowing the woman from college and claimed personal resentment from previous conflicts motivated the crime. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence, with further investigation ongoing.
title_en: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online
